subject.title: Agent confabulates completed actions on Telegram surface — same config works reliably on Claude Code/Codex

question: Should Telegram/ACP source turns enforce an action-verification or fail-closed policy when visible final text claims completed side effects without matching tool evidence?
rationale: Current main intentionally separates automatic final delivery, message_tool_only private finals, and warning-only diagnostics; changing this into verification or suppression affects privacy, compatibility, and model-behavior expectations across channel workflows.

options.title: Define verification policy
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers specify which action claims require tool-ledger evidence and what diagnostic, retry, or failure behavior should occur when evidence is missing.

options.title: Scope to stranded-final recovery
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/85714 and its recovery PR as the only current repair path, leaving broader action-claim verification out of core for now.

options.title: Document current boundary
options.body: Accept model-side false completion as an operator/model limitation and document recommended tool and hook mitigations instead of adding runtime enforcement.

recommendation.title: Define verification policy
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers specify which action claims require tool-ledger evidence and what diagnostic, retry, or failure behavior should occur when evidence is missing.

likelyOwner.reason: The current source-reply policy and private-final warning paths are attributed to this owner in local history, and the decision is about that policy boundary.
